title: अंश ४ · अध्याय ५

items.text: (निमिचरित्रम्, निमिवंशश्च)
items.tr: (nimicaritram, nimivaṃśaśca)

items.speaker: श्रीपराशर उवाच
items.text: इक्ष्वाकुतनयो योऽसौ निमिर्नाम, सहस्रं वत्सरं सत्रमारेभे ॥ १ ॥
items.tr: ikṣvākutanayo yo'sau nimirnāma, sahasraṃ vatsaraṃ satramārebhe || 1 ||

items.text: वसिष्ठं च होतारं वरयामास ॥ २ ॥
items.tr: vasiṣṭhaṃ ca hotāraṃ varayāmāsa || 2 ||

items.text: तमाह वसिष्ठः, “अहम् इन्द्रेण पञ्चवर्षशतयागार्थं प्रथमं वृतः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr: tamāha vasiṣṭhaḥ, “aham indreṇa pañcavarṣaśatayāgārthaṃ prathamaṃ vṛtaḥ || 3 ||

items.text: तदनन्तरं प्रतिपाल्यताम्, आगतः तवापि ऋत्विक् भविष्यामि” इत्युक्ते स पृथिवीपतिः न किञ्चिदुक्तवान् ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr: tadanantaraṃ pratipālyatām, āgataḥ tavāpi ṛtvik bhaviṣyāmi” ityukte sa pṛthivīpatiḥ na kiñciduktavān || 4 ||

items.text: वसिष्ठोऽप्यनेन समन्वीप्सितम् इति अमरपतेः यागम् अकरोत् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr: vasiṣṭho'pyanena samanvīpsitam iti amarapateḥ yāgam akarot || 5 ||

items.text: सोऽपि तत्काल एवान्यैः गौतमादिभिः यागमकरोत् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr: so'pi tatkāla evānyaiḥ gautamādibhiḥ yāgamakarot || 6 ||

items.text: समाप्ते चामरपतेः यागे, त्वरया वसिष्ठो निमियज्ञं करिष्यामि इत्याजगाम ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr: samāpte cāmarapateḥ yāge, tvarayā vasiṣṭho nimiyajñaṃ kariṣyāmi ityājagāma || 7 ||

items.text: तत्कर्मकर्तृत्वं च गौतमस्य दृष्ट्वा, स्वपते तस्मै राज्ञे मां प्रत्याख्याय, “एतदनेन गौतमाय कर्मान्तरं समर्पितं यस्मात् तस्मादयं विदेहो भविष्यति” इति शापं ददौ ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr: tatkarmakartṛtvaṃ ca gautamasya dṛṣṭvā, svapate tasmai rājñe māṃ pratyākhyāya, “etadanena gautamāya karmāntaraṃ samarpitaṃ yasmāt tasmādayaṃ videho bhaviṣyati” iti śāpaṃ dadau || 8 ||

items.text: प्रबुद्धश्च असौ अवनीपतिरपि प्राह ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr: prabuddhaśca asau avanīpatirapi prāha || 9 ||

items.text: “यस्मान्माम् असम्भाष्य अज्ञानत एव शयानस्य शापोत्सर्गम् असौ दुष्टगुरुः चकार, तस्मात् तस्यापि देहः पतिष्यति” इति शापं दत्त्वा देहमत्यजत् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr: “yasmānmām asambhāṣya ajñānata eva śayānasya śāpotsargam asau duṣṭaguruḥ cakāra, tasmāt tasyāpi dehaḥ patiṣyati” iti śāpaṃ dattvā dehamatyajat || 10 ||

items.text: तच्छापाच्च मित्रावरुणयोस्तेजसि वसिष्ठस्य चेतः प्रविष्टम् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr: tacchāpācca mitrāvaruṇayostejasi vasiṣṭhasya cetaḥ praviṣṭam || 11 ||

items.text: उर्वशीदर्शनात् उद्भूतबीजप्रपातयोः तयोः सकाशात् वसिष्ठो देहम् अपरं लेभे ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr: urvaśīdarśanāt udbhūtabījaprapātayoḥ tayoḥ sakāśāt vasiṣṭho deham aparaṃ lebhe || 12 ||

items.text: निमेरपि तच्छरीरम् अतिमनोहरगन्धतैलगन्धादिभिः उपसंस्क्रियमाणं नैव क्लेदादिकं दोषम् अवाप, सद्यो मृत इव तस्थौ ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr: nimerapi taccharīram atimanoharagandhatailagandhādibhiḥ upasaṃskriyamāṇaṃ naiva kledādikaṃ doṣam avāpa, sadyo mṛta iva tasthau || 13 ||

items.text: यज्ञसमाप्तौ च भागग्रहणाय देवान् आगतान् ऋत्विज ऊचुः “यजमानाय वरो दीयताम्” इति ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr: yajñasamāptau ca bhāgagrahaṇāya devān āgatān ṛtvija ūcuḥ “yajamānāya varo dīyatām” iti || 14 ||

items.text: देवैः छन्दितः असौ निमिराह ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr: devaiḥ chanditaḥ asau nimirāha || 15 ||

items.text: “भगवन्तः अखिलसंसारदुःखहन्तारः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr: “bhagavantaḥ akhilasaṃsāraduḥkhahantāraḥ || 16 ||

items.text: न ह्येतादृगन्यद् दुःखमस्ति यच्छरीरात्मनोः वियोगे भवति ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr: na hyetādṛganyad duḥkhamasti yaccharīrātmanoḥ viyoge bhavati || 17 ||

items.text: तदहमिच्छामि सकललोकलोचनेषु वस्तुं, न पुनः शरीरग्रहणं कर्तुम्” इति एवम् उक्तैः देवैः असौ अशेषभूतानां नैत्रेषु अवतारितः ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr: tadahamicchāmi sakalalokalocaneṣu vastuṃ, na punaḥ śarīragrahaṇaṃ kartum” iti evam uktaiḥ devaiḥ asau aśeṣabhūtānāṃ naitreṣu avatāritaḥ || 18 ||

items.text: ततो भूतानि उन्मेषनिमेषं चक्रुः ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr: tato bhūtāni unmeṣanimeṣaṃ cakruḥ || 19 ||

items.text: अपुत्रस्य च भूभुजः शरीरम् अराजकभीरवो मुनयो अरण्या ममन्थुः ॥ २० ॥
items.tr: aputrasya ca bhūbhujaḥ śarīram arājakabhīravo munayo araṇyā mamanthuḥ || 20 ||

items.text: तत्र च कुमारो जज्ञे ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr: tatra ca kumāro jajñe || 21 ||

items.text: जननात् जनकसंज्ञां च अवाप ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr: jananāt janakasaṃjñāṃ ca avāpa || 22 ||

items.text: अभूत् विदेहोऽस्य पिता इति वैदेहः, मथनात् मिथिः इति ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr: abhūt videho'sya pitā iti vaidehaḥ, mathanāt mithiḥ iti || 23 ||

items.text: तस्य उदावसुः पुत्रोऽभवत् ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr: tasya udāvasuḥ putro'bhavat || 24 ||

items.text: उदावसोः नन्दिवर्धनः ततः सुकेतुः, तस्मात् देवरातः, ततश्च बृहदुक्थः, तस्य च महावीर्यः, तस्यापि सुधृतिः ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr: udāvasoḥ nandivardhanaḥ tataḥ suketuḥ, tasmāt devarātaḥ, tataśca bṛhadukthaḥ, tasya ca mahāvīryaḥ, tasyāpi sudhṛtiḥ || 25 ||

items.text: ततश्च धृष्टकेतुः अजायत ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr: tataśca dhṛṣṭaketuḥ ajāyata || 26 ||

items.text: धृष्टकेतोः हर्यश्वः, तस्य च मनुः, मनोः प्रतीकः, तस्मात् कृतरथः, तस्य च देवमीढः, तस्य च विबुधो, विबुधस्य महाधृतिः, ततश्च कृतरातः, ततो महारोमा, तस्य सुवर्णरोमा, तत्पुत्रो ह्रस्वरोमा, ह्रस्वरोम्णः सीरध्वजः अभवत् ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr: dhṛṣṭaketoḥ haryaśvaḥ, tasya ca manuḥ, manoḥ pratīkaḥ, tasmāt kṛtarathaḥ, tasya ca devamīḍhaḥ, tasya ca vibudho, vibudhasya mahādhṛtiḥ, tataśca kṛtarātaḥ, tato mahāromā, tasya suvarṇaromā, tatputro hrasvaromā, hrasvaromṇaḥ sīradhvajaḥ abhavat || 27 ||

items.text: तस्य पुत्रार्थं यजनभुवं कृषतः सीरे सीता दुहिता समुत्पन्ना ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr: tasya putrārthaṃ yajanabhuvaṃ kṛṣataḥ sīre sītā duhitā samutpannā || 28 ||

items.text: सीरध्वजस्य भ्राता साङ्काश्याधिपतिः कुशध्वजनामा आसीत् ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr: sīradhvajasya bhrātā sāṅkāśyādhipatiḥ kuśadhvajanāmā āsīt || 29 ||

items.text: सीरध्वजस्य अपत्यं भानुमान्, भानुमतः, शतद्युम्नः, तस्य तु शुचिः, तस्मात् च ऊर्जनामा पुत्रो जज्ञे ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr: sīradhvajasya apatyaṃ bhānumān, bhānumataḥ, śatadyumnaḥ, tasya tu śuciḥ, tasmāt ca ūrjanāmā putro jajñe || 30 ||

items.text: तस्यापि शतध्वजः, ततः कृतिः, कृतेरञ्जनः, तत्पुत्रः कुरुजित्, ततोऽरिष्टनेमिः, तस्मात् श्रुतायुः, श्रुतायुषः सुपार्श्वः, तस्मात् सृञ्जयः, ततः क्षेमावी, क्षेमाविनोऽनेनाः, तस्मात् भौमरथः, तस्य सत्यरथः, तस्मादुपगुः, उपगोः उपगुप्तः, तत्पुत्रः स्वागतः, तस्य च सुपार्श्वः, तस्यापि सुभाषः, ततः सुश्रुतः, तस्मात् सुश्रुतात् जयः, तस्य पुत्रो विजयो, विजयस्य ऋतः, ऋतात् सुनयः सुनाद् वीतहव्यः, तस्मात् धृतिः, धृतेः बहुलाश्वः, तस्य पुत्रः कृतिः ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr: tasyāpi śatadhvajaḥ, tataḥ kṛtiḥ, kṛterañjanaḥ, tatputraḥ kurujit, tato'riṣṭanemiḥ, tasmāt śrutāyuḥ, śrutāyuṣaḥ supārśvaḥ, tasmāt sṛñjayaḥ, tataḥ kṣemāvī, kṣemāvino'nenāḥ, tasmāt bhaumarathaḥ, tasya satyarathaḥ, tasmādupaguḥ, upagoḥ upaguptaḥ, tatputraḥ svāgataḥ, tasya ca supārśvaḥ, tasyāpi subhāṣaḥ, tataḥ suśrutaḥ, tasmāt suśrutāt jayaḥ, tasya putro vijayo, vijayasya ṛtaḥ, ṛtāt sunayaḥ sunād vītahavyaḥ, tasmāt dhṛtiḥ, dhṛteḥ bahulāśvaḥ, tasya putraḥ kṛtiḥ || 31 ||

items.text: कृतौ सन्तिष्ठतेऽयं जनकवंशः ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr: kṛtau santiṣṭhate'yaṃ janakavaṃśaḥ || 32 ||
ityete maithilāḥ || 33 ||

items.text: प्रायेणैते आत्मविद्याश्रयिणो भूपाला भवन्ति ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr: prāyeṇaite ātmavidyāśrayiṇo bhūpālā bhavanti || 34 ||

en_chapter: The son of Ikshawku, by name Nimi, instituted a sacrifice for a thousand years and appointed Vasishtha as the presiding priest. Vasishtha said to him—"I have been already appointed by Indra for presiding at a sacrifice for five hundred years. Wait for some time, I shall come and officiate as a priest at your sacrifice". Being thus addressed the king did not answer. And Vasishtha went away supposing that he had agreed. Nimi in the meantime engaged Gautama and other ascetics and conducted the sacrifice. After the sacrifice of the king of celestials had been finished, Vasishtha hurried on to celebrate Nimi's sacrifice and found that it was being conducted under the superintendence of Gautama. Vasishtha then imprecated a curse upon the king who was asleep, saying "Since the king, not informing me, has entrusted Gautama with the charge of the sacrifice, he shall cease to exist in a corporeal form". When Nimi got up he came to know what had happened and in return imprecated a curse upon his unjust preceptor that he should also cease to exist in a corporeal form as the punishment of uttering a curse upon him without previously communicating with him. Nimi then gave up his bodily form. The spirit of Vasishtha, also renouncing his body, was united with the spirits of Mitra and Varuna for some time, when at last on account of their lustful desire for the nymph Urvasi he was born again in a different body. Nimi's body continued to be handsome and being embalmed with fragrant oils and resins it was not decomposed and remained like the corpse of one just dead. When the gods arrived there to receive their portion on the completion of the sacrifice the priests requested them to confer blessings upon the celebrator of the sacrifice. And being ordered by the celestials for the same Nimi said—"O celestials, you remove all ills from the world. There is not in the world a greater cause of distress than the separation of soul and body. I therefore wish to dwell in the eyes of all beings and not to take up a corporeal form any more". The celestials agreed to this and Nimi was placed by them in the eyes of all living beings and therefore their eye-lids are ever opening and shutting. As Nimi had no son the sages were afraid that the earth would have no ruler. So they churned the body of the king and a son was born who was named Janaka. As his father had no body Janaka was also called Videha. He also received the name of Mithi for having been produced by mathana or agitation. The son of Janaka was Udavasu, whose son was Nandivarddana, whose son was Suketu, whose son was Devarata, whose son was Vrihaduktha, whose son was Mahavirya, whose son was Satyadhristi, whose son was Dhrishtaketu, whose son was Haryyaswa, whose son was Maru, whose son was Pratibandhaka, whose son was Krisaratha, whose son was Krita, whose son was Vibudha, whose son was Mahadhriti, whose son was Kritirāta, whose son was Mahadhriti, whose son was Suvarnaroman, whose son was Haraswaroman, whose son was Siradhwaja.

Siradhwaja ploughing the field, to make it ready for a sacrifice which he undertook in order to obtain progeny, there sprang up in the furrow a damsel who became his daughter Sitā. The brother of Siradhwaja was Kusadhwaja who was king of Kasi. His son was named Bhanumat whose son was Satadhyumna, whose son was Suchi, whose son was Urjjavaha, whose son was Satyadwaya, whose son was Kuni, whose son was Anyana, whose son was Retujit, whose son was Arishtanemi, whose son was Srutayas, whose son was Sanjaya, whose son was Kshemari, whose son was Anenas, whose son was Minaratha, whose son was Satyaratha, whose son was Upagu, whose son was Sruta, whose son was Saswata, whose son was Sudhanwan, whose son was Subhāsa, whose son was Susruta, whose son was Jaya, whose son was Rita, whose son was Sunaya, whose son was Vitahadya, whose son was Dhriti, whose son was Bahalaswa, whose son was Kriti with whom ended the family of Janaka. These are the kings of Mithilā who shall be principally well-versed in spiritual knowledge.
